name: Mephibosheth
bio:
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul. He was five years old when news came of Saul and Jonathan's deaths at Jezreel; his nurse picked him up and fled in panic, and in her haste he fell and was crippled in both feet from then on (2 Samuel 4:4).

Years later, David asked whether anyone was left of Saul's house to whom he could show kindness for Jonathan's sake, and Saul's former servant Ziba told him of Mephibosheth, now living in the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar. David sent for him; Mephibosheth came and fell on his face before the king, and when David said his name, he answered, "Your servant" (2 Samuel 9:1-6). David told him not to be afraid, restored to him all the land that had belonged to Saul, and declared that Mephibosheth would eat at the king's own table from then on — like one of the king's sons. Mephibosheth, overwhelmed, replied, "What is your servant, that you should notice a dead dog like me?" David then assigned Ziba and his household to farm the land on Mephibosheth's behalf, while Mephibosheth himself settled in Jerusalem, eating continually at the king's table, crippled in both feet to the end (2 Samuel 9:7-13). When Absalom's rebellion forced David to flee Jerusalem, Mephibosheth's servant Ziba met David with supplies and claimed Mephibosheth had stayed behind in the city hoping to reclaim Saul's kingdom; David granted Ziba everything that had belonged to Mephibosheth on the spot. When David returned victorious, Mephibosheth came down to meet him, his feet unwashed and beard untrimmed since the day the king had left, and told a very different story: he had asked Ziba to saddle a donkey for him since he was lame, but Ziba had deceived him and slandered him to the king. Mephibosheth declared that David could do as he saw fit, since his whole family had deserved only death and yet David had given him a place at the royal table. When David, unable to settle the matter, ordered that he and Ziba divide the land between them, Mephibosheth replied that Ziba could have it all, now that the king had returned home safely (2 Samuel 19:24-30).
